title: OpenTopography - NASADEM Global Digital Elevation Model (30 m)
licence: OpenTopography's own Use License field reads verbatim: "Not Provided". The underlying NASA product page states the data is "openly shared, without restriction, in accordance with the EOSDIS Data Use and Citation Guidance".
notes: OFF-LIST site. The only shortlisted route that covers Scotland. Server-side bounding-box crop with a map selector and manual Xmin/Ymin/Xmax/Ymax entry; guest download, no account. Bit depth NOT stated on the page. OpenTopography prints a citation/acknowledgement string (NASA JPL, NASADEM Merged DEM Global 1 arc second V001, DOI https://doi.org/10.5069/G93T9FD9). The sibling SRTM GL1 30 m dataset is identical in every respect and also reads 'Use License: Not Provided'.
chosen_for: Base ground silhouette for the level. See docs/foundation-plan.md, sessions B and C.

crop_plan.intent: Crop a REAL glen roughly 2 km across and compress it into the 192 m game world. Do NOT map the real world 1:1 - at 30 m/px that would give ~6x6 samples and a featureless ramp.
crop_plan.target: Glen Coe or Glen Etive, Scottish Highlands. Wild Metal Country was made in Dundee and its landscapes read as highlands.
crop_plan.approximate_centre: Glen Coe is near 56.67 N, -5.03 E. APPROXIMATE - frame the exact crop by eye in OpenTopography's map selector, do not trust these numbers as surveyed.
crop_plan.span_arithmetic: At 56.67 N: 1 deg latitude ~= 111 km, so 2 km ~= 0.018 deg. 1 deg longitude ~= 111 * cos(56.67) ~= 61 km, so 2 km ~= 0.033 deg. A 2 km box is therefore about 0.018 deg tall and 0.033 deg wide - note it is NOT square in degrees.
crop_plan.expected_raster: ~67 x 67 px for a 2 km crop at 30 m/px.
crop_plan.vertical_warning: Real relief in Glen Coe is several hundred metres. Compressed into a world whose current terrain has ~17 m of relief (SDFHills amplitude 22), height_scale on SDFHeightmap will need to be a SMALL fraction of real - order 0.02-0.05. Tune it against Terrain.surface_height_range(), which returns measured min/max/mean, rather than guessing.

conversion_required.why: Godot reads PNG, EXR and HDR. It does NOT read GeoTIFF, IMG, Arc ASCII or HGT. A conversion sits between the download and the engine.
conversion_required.alternative: QGIS export, if GDAL is not installed standalone.
conversion_required.bit_depth: Must end up 16-bit. An 8-bit PNG gives 256 height steps and bands visibly on smooth slopes. No source page stated the input bit depth, so verify the output rather than assuming the -ot UInt16 flag had something to preserve.

licence_note: The 'Not Provided' on OpenTopography is an EMPTY FIELD on a redistributor, not a stated restriction; the underlying product is NASA's and NASA states it is openly shared without restriction. Recorded as two separate facts rather than resolved into one. OpenTopography additionally REQUESTS acknowledgement and a DOI citation - a request accompanying public-domain data, not a licence obligation. Both stated here so the decision is visible later rather than re-litigated.
